artifacts.synopsis: TE John Evans appealed Arizona Presbytery's vote to divest him of his office without censure under BCO 34-10, after he had already affiliated with the Evangelical Presbyterian Church in England and Wales and notified the Presbytery of his withdrawal. The SJC unanimously sustained the appeal and reversed the Presbytery's action, holding that Evans had withdrawn from Presbytery's jurisdiction under BCO 38-3a before the divestiture proceedings began, and instructed the Presbytery to record the irregularity, acknowledge his new membership, and remove his name from the roll.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC ruled that the Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley erred in approving a Session's erasure of a member's name from the roll under BCO 38-4 after she pled not guilty to a charge of failing to submit to church government and pursued divorce contrary to the Session's counsel. The SJC found multiple constitutional errors including improper conflation of a not-guilty plea with refusal to submit, failure to consider whether the member would fulfill vows in another branch of the church, failure to notify the member of her erasure, and proceeding to a case without process after dropping formal charges.

artifacts.title: Doty v. Nashville Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Ms. Doty and 21 others filed charges against a Nashville Presbytery teaching elder first with his congregation's Session (wrong court), then with Nashville Presbytery; Presbytery declined to indict and treated the matter as a report under BCO 31-2 rather than charges. The SJC dismissed the complaint as judicially out of order (11-9-2-2) on the ground that Doty lacked standing under BCO 43-1 as a non-member of Nashville Presbytery; a significant dissent argued that her filing of charges gave her standing under prior precedent (Lyons, Ruff, Fordice).

artifacts.synopsis: Appeal of TE Michael Chastain v. Heritage Presbytery. Chastain challenged Heritage Presbytery's judgment of guilty on charges of divisive behavior and censure of indefinite suspension from office and sacraments. The SJC sustained Presbytery's judgment, finding that Chastain's public letters to the congregation expressing disagreement with Session decisions violated his ordination vows to be subject to his brethren and maintain the peace and unity of the Church, even though his underlying views were not sinful.

artifacts.synopsis: Grace Presbyterian Church challenged Covenant Presbytery's handling of protests and complaints concerning its refusal to institute process against Daniel R. Morse and Curtis I. Crenshaw. The SJC directed that the two ministers be removed from the presbytery roll under BCO 38-3, held that Grace could withdraw under BCO 25-11 without prior notice, and recorded that Grace's complaints had been abandoned as moot.

artifacts.title: Morse v. Covenant Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission addressed three issues regarding actions of Covenant Presbytery involving TE Daniel R. Morse and Grace Presbyterian Church. The Commission ruled that teaching elders Morse and Crenshaw, having renounced communion with the PCA by joining the Reformed Episcopal Church, should be removed from presbytery rolls under BCO 38-3. The Commission found no provision requiring churches to notify presbytery before withdrawing from the PCA. Finally, the Commission determined that receiving and recording a protest is an administrative act, not a judicial decision, and that complaints regarding such actions are barred by BCO 45-5.
